scientific_hypothesis: A single-cavity structure with carefully engineered defect layers in the Bragg mirror can produce two transmission peaks without requiring two separate cavities, reducing total layer count while maintaining dual-band performance.
expected_advantages: Fewer total layers (20 vs 22) reduces stress and cost
Single-cavity may have simpler optimization landscape
Defect engineering offers finer control over peak positions
known_risks: Two peaks from single cavity may be harder to separate than dual-cavity
Defect positions sensitive to thickness errors
May produce unwanted transmission between the two target bands
expected_observations: best_target_score should increase if defect positions converge to create two distinct peaks
tightest_margin may be lower than dual-cavity routes if peak separation is challenging
valid_candidates should remain high if 20-layer topology is more manufacturable
If hypothesis fails, only one transmission peak will emerge or peaks will merge
stop_conditions: if best_target_score improves by less than 1e-3 against the historical best for two consecutive rounds, treat the axis as exhausted, stop and keep the current best
if only one transmission peak is observed in the spectrum after three rounds, defect engineering is insufficient for dual-band, stop and compare to dual-cavity routes
